title: Composables: Vue’s answer to a custom hook

videos.script:
A React developer reaches for a custom hook. A Vue developer reaches for a composable. {{what}} It is a function that uses refs, computed values, watchers and hooks, and returns some of them for a component to use. Nothing more.

You start by turning lesson seven's renderless component into one, and calling it twice for two weeks that do not share a thing.

{{rules}} Then the conventions. Accept a ref, a getter or a plain value. Return refs. And you will see what happens when a plain number is passed in.

{{fetch}} Then a composable that fetches, cancels and reports, so that no component writes that again.

{{hooks}} Then hooks inside a composable. They attach to whichever component is being set up, and to nothing at all when you call the composable from a click.

{{react}} Then the comparison with React's hooks, and why Vue has no rule about calling them in the same order.

{{planner}} And last, the planner's app hands its data and its clock to two composables, and you will see where that stops being enough.
